verses.text: Yahweh said to Noah, "Go into the ark with your whole household. I've seen that you are righteous in this generation.
Take seven pairs of every clean animal, a male and its mate. Take one pair of every animal that is not clean, a male and its mate.
Also take seven pairs of every kind of bird, male and female, so their offspring can continue across the whole earth.
In seven days I will make it rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights. I will wipe from the ground every living thing I have made."
Noah did everything Yahweh commanded him.
Noah was 600 years old when the floodwaters came on the earth.
Noah entered the ark with his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives to escape the floodwaters.
Clean animals, animals that were not clean, birds, and everything that crawls on the ground
came to Noah in pairs, male and female, just as God had commanded Noah.
After seven days, the floodwaters came over the earth.
In the 600th year of Noah's life, on the seventeenth day of the second month, all the springs of the great deep burst open, and the windows of the sky opened.
Rain poured on the earth for forty days and forty nights.
That same day Noah entered the ark with Shem, Ham, and Japheth—his sons—along with his wife and the three wives of his sons.
They brought in every kind of wild animal, livestock, creature that crawls on the ground, and bird.
Pairs of every living creature that breathes came to Noah inside the ark.
Every kind entered male and female, just as God had commanded Noah. Then Yahweh shut the door behind him.
The flood kept coming for forty days. The waters rose and lifted the ark up above the earth.
The waters kept rising and grew powerful over the earth, and the ark floated on the surface.
The waters rose so high that every tall mountain under the whole sky was covered.
The water rose fifteen cubits above the mountains, covering them.
Every living creature that moved on the earth died—the birds, livestock, wild animals, creatures crawling on the ground, and human beings.
Everything on dry land that had the breath of life in its nostrils died.
Every living thing on the ground was wiped out: people, livestock, crawling creatures, and birds. Only Noah and those with him in the ark survived.
The floodwaters covered the earth for 150 days.
